Central Member Appeals Processing
Healthy Blue
P.O. Box 62429
Virginia Beach, VA 23466-2429

Date: August 20, 2026

**RE: NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION APPEAL**
*   **Member:** Rowan Novak
*   **Member ID:** W671638429
*   **Plan:** Healthy Blue Louisiana (Commercial/ACA)
*   **Reference Number:** POC-7CD7D16B79-75735
*   **Requested Service:** Partial Knee Replacement (Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty)
*   **CPT Code:** 27446
*   **Provider:** Dr. Okafor, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
*   **Date of Denial Notice:** August 16, 2026
*   **Appeal Deadline:** February 12, 2027 (180 days from notice)

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal Healthy Blue Louisiana’s denial of prior authorization for my requested partial knee replacement (unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, CPT 27446) to be performed by Dr. Okafor. 

The denial letter dated August 16, 2026, states that “the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.” This determination is clinically incorrect and directly contradicts my medical records. The clinical packet submitted by Dr. Okafor’s office clearly documents that I have not only undergone but have failed an exhaustive, multi-modality conservative treatment program that far exceeds the requirements of the plan's governing medical policy, **Healthy Blue Medical Policy CAM 775HB** (which aligns with the Carelon Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria for Joint Surgery, **Doc ID: MSK02-1125.1**).

Below, I map the specific criteria set forth in the plan's governing policy to my actual clinical documentation, demonstrating full medical necessity.

### 1. The Policy Bypasses Conservative Care When Bone-on-Bone Articulation Is Present
Under the plan’s policy, medial or lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty is considered medically necessary when certain criteria are met. Crucially, the policy states:
> "Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present, failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following..."

My objective imaging results prove that bone-on-bone articulation is actively present:
*   **Imaging (2026-06-20):** An MRI of my [left/right] knee reveals **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition** and **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 degeneration** localized medially.
*   Because bone-on-bone articulation is objectively documented on my MRI, the requirement for a trial of conservative management is technically bypassed under your own guidelines.

### 2. If Evaluated, the Conservative Treatment Trial Was Fully Completed and Failed
Even if Healthy Blue requires the clinical trial of conservative management, my medical records document that I have completed a rigorous, 14-week conservative care trial that satisfies and exceeds the policy's requirements.

The policy lists the following non-operative treatment modalities (requiring at least TWO):
*   > "- Physical therapy modalities"
*   > "- Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics"
*   > "- Injections: corticosteroid or viscosupplementation"

My clinical records document successful trial and failure of **three** of these modalities over a period spanning more than 12 weeks:
1.  **Supervised Physical Therapy:** From March 22, 2026, to June 28, 2026 (a duration of **14 weeks**), I completed **20 visits** of supervised physical therapy focusing on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. This is fully documented in the attached physical therapy discharge note.
2.  **Pharmacologic Treatment:** I utilized prescription-strength oral NSAIDs daily for **4 months** with completely inadequate pain relief. 
3.  **Intra-articular Injection:** On May 7, 2026, I received a therapeutic corticosteroid injection in the affected joint, which provided only two weeks of partial pain relief before my symptoms returned to baseline.

### 3. All Other Clinical Criteria are Fully Satisfied
The plan's policy lists additional criteria, all of which are met:
*   **Pain Duration:** The policy requires > "At least 12 weeks of pain localized to the medial or lateral compartment". My records document **18 months** of progressive, severe, and unrelieved pain localized to the medial compartment of my [left/right] knee.
*   **Injection Timing:** The policy mandates > "No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery". My single intra-articular corticosteroid injection occurred on **May 7, 2026**. Because this injection was administered more than 12 weeks prior to any currently scheduled surgery date, this timing criterion is met.
*   **Surgical History:** The policy mandates > "No prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery". I have had no knee surgeries within the last 6 months.
*   **Clinical Status:** I have a BMI of 29, am a non-smoker, have no active local or systemic infections, and have no untreated substance use issues. 

### Conclusion
My joint disease is severe, and it restricts my essential activities of daily living. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake up 3 to 4 times every night due to severe joint pain. 

Because my records clearly document a failed 14-week course of physical therapy, 4 months of failed NSAID therapy, a failed corticosteroid injection, and objective MRI evidence of medial bone-on-bone joint space narrowing (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4), I meet every medical necessity requirement for CPT 27446 under policy CAM 775HB / MSK02-1125.1. 

I request that Healthy Blue Louisiana immediately reverse this denial and authorize the partial knee replacement as requested by Dr. Okafor. Please feel free to contact me or Dr. Okafor’s office if any further clinical documentation is required. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent medical appeal.

Sincerely,

Rowan Novak  
[Patient Signature]  
[Patient Phone Number]  
[Patient Address]
